caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: Liberia's debt was among the world's most extreme before relief: 450.9% of GDP in 2006, the series high. HIPC/MDRI completion in 2010 brought it down to 20.5% by 2012, the series low. Since then it has climbed steadily as post-Ebola and post-commodity-boom governments borrowed for reconstruction: 55.2% projected for 2025. The debt is mostly concessional, and IMF assessments judge the risk of distress moderate, but the trajectory is a warning: Liberia has re-accumulated in fifteen years a quarter of what took decades to forgive, without building the revenue base to service it comfortably.
inflation_management: Liberia's inflation is driven by the Liberian dollar's depreciation and import dependence, with partial dollarization limiting monetary traction. It ran at 17.5% in 2008 on the global food-fuel crisis, then moderated to 6.8% by 2012, the series low. The 2018-19 currency crisis, as the central bank printed money amid scandal, sent inflation to 23.5% and a series high of 27.0% in 2019. Tighter policy and IMF support stabilized it around 7-10% from 2021, with 8.3% projected for 2025. The central bank has no formal inflation target and limited instruments; exchange-rate stability is the de facto objective, and it has been elusive.

key_events.event: HIPC completion-point relief cut debt from 450.9% to about 20% of GDP.
Ebola epidemic killed thousands and devastated the economy.
George Weah won the presidency, succeeding Ellen Johnson Sirleaf.
Currency crisis: central bank money-printing scandals pushed inflation to 27.0%.
COVID-19; IMF program supported the response.
Joseph Boakai defeated Weah in the November 2023 runoff, a democratic transfer.

outlook_next_decade: The base case is slow IMF-anchored stabilization with inflation near 8% and debt around 55% of GDP. Upside comes from mining (iron ore) and agriculture if governance improves; downside is that the debt trajectory continues toward distress and another currency crisis. Uncertainty is moderate-to-high: the 2023 transfer was peaceful, but state capacity is extremely thin and the economy remains aid-dependent.
